findings.title: Poisoning detection cannot see collisions outside the request, so a wrong cost can be attributed
findings.location: design.md §5.2 point 3, §6.6 algorithm steps 2-3, §9.4 invariant row 2, criterion 25d
findings.problem: The join's central soundness claim is that an identifier claimed by two ACTIVE rows with distinct ARNs is poisoned and never used. The stated algorithm reads the inventory once, via rowsFor(cloudAccountId, requestedIds), and that query (WHERE cloudAccountId = :id AND (arn IN :ids OR resourceId IN :ids), verified in AwsCloudResourceRepository) returns only rows matching a requested id. A second resource sharing the first resource's short id is absent from the result set unless that short id is itself requested, so step 3 sees one claimant and emits the colliding short id as a candidate. Requesting arn:aws:rds:...:db:prod alone therefore puts 'prod' into the IN list, and any CUR row written under the bare id 'prod' for a different resource is summed into this one. §5.2's own example ('requesting the two ARNs of the xammer-prod pair prices both correctly') works only because both ARNs are in one request, which hides the gap.
findings.fix: Add a second inventory read between steps 2 and 3 and build the poison index from the union: rows = rowsFor(acct, requestedIds); claimants = rowsFor(acct, rows.map(getResourceId).filter(non-blank)); poisonIndex over rows UNION claimants. One extra chunked call to the same repository method, index-served once the NFR-1 migration lands (which that makes required, not optional). State that ARNs need no second pass because uq_aws_cloud_resource_cloudacct_arn makes an ARN single-claimant by construction. Add AwsCloudResourceRepository to §6.2's file table if a dedicated count query is preferred. Extend criterion 25d: request only arn:aws:rds:...:db:prod with a second ACTIVE row sharing resource_id='prod'; assert 'prod' is absent from allCandidates(), the ARN still prices, and the id is NOT in ambiguous.

findings.title: A tombstone never poisons yet still supplies its short id, so a live resource absorbs a deleted resource's charges
findings.location: design.md §5.2 point 3 (four-bullet asymmetry), §6.6 steps 3 and 4b, criterion 25e bullet 1, §9.4 invariant row 3
findings.problem: The design holds that a DELETED row never poisons an identifier because a resource that no longer exists cannot be the one being asked about, and simultaneously that a DELETED row may supply candidates because a resource deleted mid-month still carries that month's CUR rows. The second statement is the counter-example to the first: if the deleted resource has CUR rows under the shared short id, a live resource sharing that id is priced with them. Criterion 25e bullet 1 asserts this as correct ('price the ACTIVE row's identifiers', plural, including the colliding short id). Result: a wrong figure, which FR-11 and §9.4 forbid. Example: live RDS db:prod (ACTIVE) plus an S3 bucket 'prod' deleted on the 9th -> the bucket's month-to-date spend lands on the RDS row.
findings.fix: Split the rule by what it governs. In §6.6 step 3: (a) an identifier claimed by >= 2 rows with distinct ARNs, ANY status, is dropped from every candidate list and never reaches the IN predicate; (b) a REQUESTED id is reported in ambiguous only when >= 2 of its claimants are ACTIVE, which preserves the no-false-apology goal; (c) a tombstone that is the only claimant still supplies both identifiers, so mid-month-delete pricing keeps working. Rewrite criterion 25e bullet 1: ACTIVE row A plus distinct-ARN DELETED row B sharing resource_id='prod' -> A prices from its ARN only, 'prod' is absent from the IN list, A is not in ambiguous. Bullets 2-4 stand.

findings.title: A poisoned requested id renders state 2 (no retry) for a resource that is in the topology
findings.location: design.md §6.3 ResourceIdentities response shape, §6.6 step 4a and step 5, §8.3 rootNodeId, §8.5 state 2, criterion 25b
findings.problem: nodeIdCandidates comes from CurIdentifiers.byRequestedId, and step 4a gives a poisoned requested id NO candidates (criterion 25b confirms an empty list). In §8.3 that makes both match passes iterate an empty array, so rootNodeId is null and §8.5 renders state 2, 'This resource is not in the account topology', the one state with no retry control. The statement is false and unrecoverable: ResourceIdentities carries only (identities, requested, resolved) with no ambiguous field, so the client cannot tell 'the server refused to resolve this' from 'no candidate matched a node'. It is reachable because the drawer's resourceId is a CUR id, which for every bare-id type is exactly the short form poisoning operates on, and the demo fixtures already contain the collision (db:xammer-prod vs cluster/xammer-prod). This is the same false-benign-state failure §14 item 1 and §15 finding 3 were written to eliminate, arriving by a path neither covers.
findings.fix: Pick one and state it. (a) Preferred: add ambiguous: string[] to ResourceIdentities (the field already exists on CurIdentifiers, so it is one line in ResourceCostJoin.identities) and add a sixth unavailable state between 1a and 2 -- 'More than one live resource in this account is called <id>, so XamOps cannot say which one this row is. The other tabs are unaffected.' -- with no retry. (b) Alternative: emit the requested id as its own nodeIdCandidates entry even when poisoned, on the stated ground that matching a node attaches no money (FR-11 constrains the cost predicate only); if chosen, say so explicitly and decide in one sentence whether rooting on a possibly-wrong node is acceptable given the header and the FR-4 focus id. Either way add a criterion: an identity entry with an empty nodeIdCandidates renders neither state 2 nor a blank screen.

findings.title: The cost query has no gating condition, so first open issues two Athena queries
findings.location: design.md §8.6 (CUR queries use 'active ? accountId : null'), §8.5, FR-10, NFR-1, criterion 5
findings.problem: The only stated enable condition for the costs query is active ? accountId : null. While the graph query is in flight, flow is null and peers is empty, so sent is [focusCostId] and the enabled query runs: one Athena query for the focus alone. When the graph lands, sent changes, the key changes (§8.6 puts the id set in the key) and a second query runs for the real peer set. That contradicts FR-10 ('one batch cost query per rendered peer set'), NFR-1 ('one Athena query per focus change') and criterion 5 ('called exactly once per focus'), and the wasted query is a full single-month partition scan. §8.5 implies the right behaviour ('costs load separately and later') without specifying a mechanism.
findings.fix: State the costs query's enable condition in §8.6 beside the other two, derived from the settled flag §8.5 already defines: const costsReady = active && settled && focusId !== null && flow !== null; then useCurInsight(costKey, costsReady ? accountId : null, period, ...). Extend criterion 5: with the identity resolving before the graph, the cost fetcher is still called exactly once.

findings.title: costsLoading excludes the no-peer case, so a peerless focus card claims 'no cost attributable' while its cost is in flight
findings.location: design.md §8.5 (costsLoading includes peerIds.length > 0), §8.4 focus-card cost, §8.5 blank-cost table, FR-8
findings.problem: The focus card's figure comes from the same batch response as the peers' (FR-4) and state 3a still renders the focus card, but costsLoading is false whenever peerIds.length === 0. For a resource with no connections the money slot therefore has no placeholder while the query runs, and the rule 'id absent from costs and ambiguous -> no cost attributable' fires against data === undefined. This is the 'in flight is not failure' error FR-8 and §8.5 eliminate on the graph axis, repeated on the cost axis.
findings.fix: Drop the peer-count clause and gate on the same condition as the query: const costsLoading = costsReady && costsQuery.isPending. State the rendering rule as: a row (focus or peer) renders the blank sentence only once the costs query has SETTLED and its sent id is absent from both costs and ambiguous. Criterion: while the costs query is pending on a zero-peer resource, the focus card shows the pricing placeholder and the string 'no cost attributable' appears nowhere.

findings.title: The graph useQuery's staleTime and retry are unspecified; project defaults contradict NFR-1 and double the cold-read wait
findings.location: design.md §8.6 (direct useQuery with only an enabled option), NFR-1, §8.8 (the 110 s derivation)
findings.problem: lib/queryClient.ts sets staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000 and retry: 1 app-wide (verified). The CUR queries escape both because useCurInsight overrides them; the graph query is a bare useQuery and inherits them. Two stated properties then fail: NFR-1 and §8.6 promise one graph request per account and region per 30-minute stale window (it would be 5 minutes, six times the vpcId=ALL builds NFR-1 is costed against); and §8.8 derives 110 s so a cold scan fails deterministically from a client-side abort, but retry: 1 retries that abort, so the reader waits ~220 s before state 1a under a sentence promising 'up to a minute', and a second account scan starts on a backend that already failed to finish one.
findings.fix: Declare the options where the query is declared: useQuery({ queryKey: ['cost-connectivity','graph', accountId ?? '', region ?? ''], queryFn: ..., enabled: active && Boolean(accountId), staleTime: 30 * 60 * 1000, retry: false }) -- with comments naming the two defaults being overridden (5 min, retry 1) so the override is not removed later as noise.

findings.title: Two sections disagree on what a non-array graph body does
findings.location: design.md §8.8 (fetcher returns [] for a non-array body, 'treated as state 1a by the caller') vs §8.5 state 1a and §9.2 row 2
findings.problem: §8.8 has the fetcher resolve [] for a non-array body; §8.5 and §9.2 both require that case to render state 1a with a Try again control and a console.warn. If the fetcher resolves [], the query is isSuccess with data.length === 0 and the ordering block reaches elements.length === 0 -> state 1b with a Reload topology control. No channel exists for the caller to learn the body was malformed, so 'treated as state 1a by the caller' is not expressible and an implementer must pick between two different sentences and two different controls.
findings.fix: Throw on a non-array body and keep [] for a genuinely empty array: const body = await response.json().catch(() => null); if (!Array.isArray(body)) { console.warn('[cloudmap] Unexpected graph body from', url); throw new Error('cloudmap/graph: unexpected shape'); } return body; -- then delete §8.8's last sentence. A 200 carrying HTML is a malformed answer (1a); an empty array is the backend's own collapsed-failure path (1b). The split stays clean.

findings.title: join can return a requested id whose summed cost is zero, which renders $0.00
findings.location: design.md §6.7 (join sums every owning candidate), §6.5 (HAVING ABS(SUM(cost)) > 0.001), FR-3, §8.5 blank-cost table, §9.4 ('No missing cost ever renders as $0.00')
findings.problem: The HAVING drops a GROUP that nets to zero; it cannot drop a REQUESTED ID that nets to zero across two surviving groups -- exactly the case §6.7 relies on ('rows written under a bare id early in the month and under an ARN later'). A charge under one form and an offsetting credit under the other (+X and -X, each above the threshold) sums to ~0. The client's rule keys on ABSENCE from costs, so a present-and-zero entry renders $0.00, the one figure FR-3 forbids, and pricedCount disagrees because it counts only ids that received a non-zero figure.
findings.fix: Drop it in join, where the arithmetic lives, so the client rule stays 'absence implies sentence': if (Math.abs(summed) <= 0.001) continue; // not added to costs, not counted in pricedCount -- with the same comment as the HAVING. Add a unit criterion beside 22a: one requested id with two candidate groups of +5.00 and -5.00 returns no costs entry, pricedCount 0, and is not listed in ambiguous.

findings.title: The trail reset is an effect, so the first render after a resource change shows the previous resource's flow
findings.location: design.md §8.6 (everActive 'cannot inherit the previous one's trail'), §8.7 (useEffect on resourceId), §8.9 item 3, criterion 18
findings.problem: ResourceCostDrawer stays mounted across resourceId changes (verified: only the portal content is gated on resourceId, and tab is already reset in useEffect(..., [resourceId])). Effects run after render, and a child's effects run before the parent's, so on the render in which resourceId changes, tab is still 'connectivity', everActive.current is still true and trail still holds the previous resource's hops: the body renders the previous resource's flow and keys its cost query off the previous focus before the reset lands. The stated guarantee is false for one commit, and criterion 18 asserts post-effect state so it would pass anyway.
findings.fix: Make the reset structural rather than an effect: render <ResourceConnectivityTab key={resourceId} active={active} ... /> inside the <div hidden={!active}> wrapper, which discards trail, expanded and scroll position synchronously, and drop everActive from the resourceId effect. Extend criterion 18: on the first render after resourceId changes, the tab body renders no peer row belonging to the previous resource and the cost fetcher is not called with the previous focus id.

findings.title: Sort and dedupe placement relative to the trim is stated in three places and assembled in none
findings.location: design.md §8.4 (drop from the end of the rendered order), §8.6 (sorted and deduplicated before the request is built), §8.7 (trimmed, then sorted, then keyed)
findings.problem: Only §8.7's ordering is consistent with §8.4 -- sorting first would destroy the rendered order the trim is defined against -- and the three statements leave an implementer to reconcile them.
findings.fix: Say it once, on trimCostIds: it consumes and returns MODEL order, and the caller sorts and dedupes 'sent' afterwards; note that sorting cannot change join(',').length so the total-length measurement is unaffected, and that the count limit applies after dedupe so a duplicate cannot consume one of the 100 slots.

findings.title: The ResourceConnectivityFlow / shorten refactor has no coverage and no acceptance criterion
findings.location: design.md §8.2 (moving TypeIcon, hueFor, hoverText; extracting shorten), §13 ('no behaviour change, no visual change')
findings.problem: All three helpers are module-private in a 1,400-line component (verified: shorten(id, max = 34) at ResourceConnectivityFlow.tsx:132, shorten(id, max = 72) at ServiceResourcesDrawer.tsx:242), and there is no test file for ResourceConnectivityFlow or connectivityFlowModel (components/CloudMap has only layout, canvasTheme and cardStyle tests). Nothing asserts §13's promise.
findings.fix: Either add one smoke criterion -- a render of ResourceConnectivityFlow over demoCloudMapGraph produces the same peer rows, glyph types and title strings as before the move -- or state explicitly that the move is covered by the type-checker alone and accept that.

findings.title: The cache-key length warning is specified twice, differently
findings.location: design.md §9.1 table ('WARN once per key') vs §9.1 prose ('One logger.warn guarded on key.length() > 255, inside store')
findings.problem: Once-per-key needs a Set, which is new state in a shared service; the prose describes an unconditional guarded warn. The two are different changes to CurInsightCache.
findings.fix: Keep the unconditional guarded warn and delete 'once per key'. Add a comment beside the literal 255 pointing at §12.2 item 4, since that item says the live column width is unverified per environment.

findings.title: The assembled cache key is shorter than §6.4 estimates
findings.location: design.md §6.4 ('roughly ... ~200 characters'), §12.2 item 4 ('that margin is thin')
findings.problem: PREFIX (13) + account (12) + '::' + 'resource-costs/' + account + '?period=YYYY-MM' + '&basis=unblended' + '&ids=' + 64 hex is ~154 characters against varchar(255), not ~200, so the follow-up's urgency is overstated.
findings.fix: Replace the estimate with the arithmetic; keep criterion 25c's suffix assertion as the guard.

findings.title: Peer order is alphabetical by relation, not by label
findings.location: design.md §8.3 and §8.4 ('declared before inferred, then alphabetical')
findings.problem: The model sorts Number(a.derived) - Number(b.derived) || a.relation.localeCompare(b.relation) (connectivityFlowModel.ts:1250). It matters because §8.4 justifies dropping from the end of that order as keeping the more informative half of the list.
findings.fix: Name the field: 'declared before inferred, then alphabetical by relation'.

findings.title: The identity answer is keyed by period, which it does not depend on
findings.location: design.md §8.6 (identities via useCurInsight), §6.3 (endpoint takes no period)
findings.problem: useCurInsight puts period ?? 'current' in the query key (verified), so changing the month on the cost page refetches an identity answer that cannot have changed.
findings.fix: Either note the harmless extra ~10 ms read, or pass period: undefined for that one query and say why.

findings.title: The resource-change skeleton still renders above the connectivity body
findings.location: design.md §8.9 items 1 and 2, ResourceCostDrawer.tsx (the '{loading && <five pulse bars>}' block)
findings.problem: §8.9 removes the 'No detail available' apology from the connectivity path and says the body is not gated on loading, but the skeleton block above it is untouched, so selecting Connectivity while the resource-change query is in flight renders five grey bars above a working flow.
findings.fix: Apply the same shape as item 1: {loading && tab !== 'connectivity' && ...}.
